title: Payment Arrangements — Re-aging Deferral of a Pre-Suspension Missed Installment
content:
## The rule in force

The re-aging deferral re-ages the installment carrying a plan's most recent missed entry from before a hardship suspension, and it is recorded once with the regular installment amount after the change.

The deferral places the re-aged installment one period after the plan's current final installment; where the re-aged remainder is spread, that installment carries only what the arrangement balance still leaves after the installments before it, the last installment absorbing the difference as the final installment absorbs rounding at set-up.

The re-aging deferral is recorded only after the plan's status is active again after its suspension.

In terms of the plan record: while a plan that was suspended does not yet show active status again, the re-aging deferral is not recorded.

This applies to plans under Payment Arrangements that were suspended for a hardship hold and carry a missed entry from before that suspension.

## What the deferral does

Ridgeline records one granted deferral on the arrangement's installment history: the named installment is moved to one period after the arrangement's current final installment, the installment after it becomes the next one due on its scheduled date, the final due date becomes the moved installment's new due date, and the regular installment amount is set to the amount given. The consumer can afterwards see the moved installment's new due date, the next due installment and the regular installment amount on the arrangement.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `reage_missed_installment_128922de`. It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_id` | The payment plan reference number (the identifier) of the arrangement, as returned by the payment arrangement lookup for the consumer | Identifier string |
| `installment_number` | The number of the installment that is re-aged | Non-negative integer |
| `installment_amount` | The regular installment amount after the change | USD, a decimal number rounded to 2 decimal places |

## Return

On success the tool returns a record rendered as text with `deferral_reference` (the reference of the deferral recorded), `plan_id`, `installment_number`, `new_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the moved installment's due date), `next_installment`, `next_due_date` (YYYY-MM-DD), `installment_amount` (USD) and `status`, always `deferral_recorded`, which shows the deferral is recorded.

When no arrangement matches the reference given, the tool returns "No payment plan found for" followed by that reference, and nothing is recorded.

## Illustration (hypothetical values)

On a monthly arrangement whose final installment is due 15 November, naming installment 6 with an amount of 212.00 returns a new due date of 15 December for installment 6, installment 7 as the next installment on its scheduled date, and 212.00 as the regular installment.
